answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by selling admission, not names. Each epoch the ledger opens a single inlet and accepts at most one new working identity; the winning bid of at least 50 POA stays locked in a vault for three epoch closes and is published as that identity's anchor, which every peer attestation must cite. Opening a second name means winning a later auction and locking a fresh deposit, so a farm of N identities pays N sequential winning bids and keeps N deposits frozen. If two answers cite the same vault deposit, both are rejected and the deposit is slashed.
